ep_title: When Did Seduction Become so Untrue? EPx16 Vol. 02 ䷶ KNOWsutra Flamenco Techno
description: This EPx16 crosses the symbolic mark of 1000 original tracks released on SoundCloud, in one year. So, YAY. It's worth acknowledging, because I am just sooo grateful for being able to process my feelings with songs. And god knows there is indeed much to process, in a world gone bananas. I considered making the 1000th track special, but I’m not that special, really ;)  This is Vol. 02 of a song I love, “How do Kids Learn Now?” aka “When did seduction become so Untrue?”, a sonic question mark wrapped in 16-track Flamenco Techno journey made of lit Gipsy soul, Arabesk minimalism, flamenco fire, and wonder… asking: What are we teaching? Who profits from forgetting? What is lost when respect is mocked and liberty becomes a loophole? And why (TF) should we care?  This song is yet another opportunity and invitation to embrace reflection and growth, to help us understand and navigate a world where perspectives differ… With hypnotic claps, poetic whispers of truth in rhythm. KNOWsutra songs are my philosophical foundation, and intended to invite wonder, and self-reflection, even when it's uncomfortable—vs. retreat and deny. It asks questions that matter, with an emphasis the importance of kids being able to learn how to differentiate rights from wrongs—as required to foster trust, and a long-term peaceful, sustainable, harmonious future, for everyone on planet Earth.  It matters to me because my faith, my commitment to kindness and honesty, is a significant part of who I am, and I care to understand who we are as humans, and how we can positively impact the world around us, to make it a better place… In a society where the moral compass is so blurred, covert narcissists charlatans like #robertgreen make  millions of dollars selling a book that teaches the  “The Art of Seduction” literally means “The Art of Manipulation” aka Deception, a reality where power grab and control have come to matter more than integrity, humility, and trust… despite what all regarded history, philosophy, economy, sociology, psychology, and of course poetry scholars know—which is that being vulnerable is being brave, because peace grows from trust, and trust relies on honesty, quite simply.  — @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] How do kids learn respect and fraternity? Morality means we agree on rights and wrongs, can’t you see? Liberty now means no accountability, The new victors boast, proud in their spree.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Verse 2] Selling lies, saying attraction’s just a ruse, Deceit for dollars, making souls confused. Boasting takers, proud of deceit, But what’s the cost, where does truth meet?  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Bridge] We need to find the way back, clear and pure, Teach kids respect, make fraternity sure. Stand for liberty, rewrite the tale, Bring back values, let truth prevail.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Outro] Restore the values, end manipulation’s reign, Teach respect, embrace compassion again.

description: Two sister-songs, with lyrics directly inspired by Dr. Ramani’s video “Narcissism: The Secondhand Smoke of Mental Health” (on YouTube)...  Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro] Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke. It’s about cocksure egos. Ha. Ready? Down we go.  [Verse 1] No mirror inside, so they borrow your face, Validation’s the drug they chase. Shiny cars, hollow eyes, Charm that blinds, and charm that lies.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Verse 2] Entitled thrones on borrowed ground, Their laughter’s loud, their silence profound. Grand illusions, paper crowns, Lift you up, then tear you down.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Bridge] No empathy, no remedy, Woke ain’t like smoke, ain’t your enemy. Round and round, the blowers spin, And sorrow seeps through my skin.  [Outro] Step away, darling, break the spell, Breathe your own air, and breathe it well. Leave their circus, let them choke,  On their own secondhand smoke.  --- SIDE B EPx3: "Arrogant hearts"  [Verse 1] Step right up to the mirror maze, Where charm is cheap and love decays, They smile so wide while they cut you thin, Secondhand smoke seeps under your skin.   [Chorus] No empathy, no remedy, Entitlement is their melody, Grandiose ghosts on high ego stage, Arrogant hearts and their puppets cage.   [Verse 2] Superficial saints with a selfie crown, Validation junkies shake you down, Malice erupts when masks won’t stay, Gaslight fever keeps truth at bay.   [Bridge] “Ladies and gents, beware the show! They’ll promise excellence, deliver shadow. Communal halos, malignant schemes, Covert whispers, grandiose dreams!”  [Final Chorus] Learned helplessness in smoky air, You breathe their poison unaware, The crowd applauds, the tyrant grins, But emptiness echoes where soul cannot sing.

Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro] Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke. It’s about cocksure egos. Ha. Ready? Down we go.  [Verse 1] No mirror inside, so they borrow your face, Validation’s the drug they chase. Shiny cars, hollow eyes, Charm that blinds, and charm that lies.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Verse 2] Entitled thrones on borrowed ground, Their laughter’s loud, their silence profound. Grand illusions, paper crowns, Lift you up, then tear you down.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Bridge] No empathy, no remedy, Woke ain’t like smoke, ain’t your enemy. Round and round, the blowers spin, And sorrow seeps through my skin.  [Outro] Step away, darling, break the spell, Breathe your own air, and breathe it well. Leave their circus, let them choke,  On their own secondhand smoke.  --- SIDE B EPx3: "Arrogant hearts"  [Verse 1] Step right up to the mirror maze, Where charm is cheap and love decays, They smile so wide while they cut you thin, Secondhand smoke seeps under your skin.   [Chorus] No empathy, no remedy, Entitlement is their melody, Grandiose ghosts on high ego stage, Arrogant hearts and their puppets cage. description: DEFY is a soul-deep, whispered scream BLOWsutra EP in 7 Tracks, which started with one question: “What are we doing?”  That’s the question @defiance13 asked in a heartfelt #TikTok monologue that cracked something in me. He was not being not rhetorical—he was being real. Caring. Conscious. Raw. Clear. Bright. Informed. Logical. Ethical. Philosophical. Outraged. Defiant. And I weeped, silently, in empathy. He sounded like Hope, with a capital H, like, just Human.  This EP is what came out of sitting with that question. Not answers, but grief. Not slogans, but songs.Three core truths, seven different renderings of them—raw and low, no sweetening. Just me, my conscience, and my lyrics. Because lyrics matter. Because denial is poison. Because silence isn’t neutral. And defiance ain’t optional.  The first song [track 1-2], “Shameless,” opens with the bitter contrast between past fascism and its modern American rebrand. Because that’s right, back then, the horrors were hidden—curtained, whispered, denied. Now? They’re streamed in HD with hashtags and lawn chairs. Cages rise from the swamp, and people cheer for suffering like it’s a half-time show. It’s not about subtle policies or gray areas, it’s about social media. It’s a freaks spectacle, people who decorate detention centers with patriotism.  The second song [track 3-5], “Optics of Cruelty,” calls out the calculated aesthetics of power. It’s not a glitch—it’s the blueprint. As the original monologue says, “You’re not witnessing the echoes of history, you’re watching its reanimation.” This track goes straight into the rot of performance-based fascism. It names names, connects dots, quotes sources, maps connections, and asks: when did control become our national art form? When did cruelty become a campaign style?  And the third [track 6-7], “Universal Currency,” is the hardest to sing. It’s a quiet scream for the children—those who die in floods, in heat, in systems designed to forget them. It’s about how this country penciled out the price of a child’s life—just under $109,000—and still dared to call it justice. But children are not budget lines. They’re our only true wealth. And the exchange rate is human decency.  Each version of these songs brings out a slightly different truth—one more bluesy, one more folk, one more hypnotic or theatrical. They’re not remixes. They’re re-feelings. This is not background music. It’s not a brand. It’s basically just my gut’s voice... And if you're wondering too, what (TF) are we doing, then maybe these songs are for you too. Because defiance, when nothing else is left, is love’s last language.  ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰   Lyrics gladly shared upon request.

description: A (few variations of a) song dedicated to all truth-tellers (some of them born gay) victims of dictatorial oppression, with much love... vive la Vérité, vive la Résistance!  "(I Wanted to Be a) Poem" is an experimental jazzy psychedelic song I wrote around the quote “I thought I wanted to be a poet but basically, I wanted to be the poem”; it is lyrically structured after the song “Summertime”, and directly inspired by the following essay about Jaime Gil de Biedma—an introverted, humble poet who lived under the Franco dictatorship, during the Spanish Inquisition (early last century)…  - “Perhaps poetry is best minted under pressure. Poetry that lasts. (...)  Jaime Gil de Biedma lived under Franco. Born in 1929 in Barcelona, Biedma was six when Federico Garcia Lorca was killed by Franco’s troops in Granada. Famously, the story goes that as they shot Lorca his murderers said: “Three shots in the ass for Garcia Lorca for being a faggot.” His body was never found. (…)  Silence carves these poems. He wrote his poems under a dictator who was famous for saying, “You are master of what you don’t say.” Maybe all poems are carved by silence. Think Dickinson. Think Hopkins. Silence can equal life. Here silence is particularly historic in a way it no longer is. Franco shut Spain up. The ground rich with unidentified corpses. Homosexuality denied in a regime that aligned itself with the conservative Catholic Church.  But poetry. Poetry provides a passport to transcendence when pressures seem unsurmountable: and more than thrice a poetry created under pressure in silence trumps death.  As Biedma began to put pen to paper, what preceded him was daunting. All the major poets had vanished: Machado on a death march, Lorca shot, Hernandez dead in prison, Cernuda fled to Mexico and never returned. Decades rolled on, censorship reigned, and torpid inertia smothered art. (...)  Poetry remains indestructible. Poetry outlasts Franco and AIDS. So long as men and women can breathe museums will preserve artifacts and a poet like Biedma will add to the record of what life was like under oppression.”

description: EPx3 - VOL. 02  Robert Burns wrote “A Man’s a Man for A’ That” over 200 years ago, and guess what… not much has changed! In fact, it is statistically fair to say that the socio—economical divide is getting worse everyday, because greedy and entitled a-holes confuse privilege with rights, and don’t even think twice about the meaning or value of equality, human dignity, and justice. Blessed be Burns for daring to say what few would: wealth and status mean nothing—what truly matters is a person’s integrity, wisdom, and kindness. Personality, aka our “true color”, is so underrated…   Why his song matters: - In an era of rising inequality, where wealth and fame often overshadow true worth, Burns’ words remind us that status does not define a person. - As leaders and elites gain power through privilege, not merit, his message calls us to value wisdom, honesty, and justice above empty authority. - In a world that too often divides people by class, race, or borders, A Man’s a Man for A’ That stands as a timeless call for fairness, unity, and human dignity.  Burns saw beyond his time and envisioned a world where honor and intelligence, not gold and crowns, define greatness. That dream isn’t just history—it’s still worth singing for. Maybe now more than ever.  -- Robert Burns’s original lyrics: (Original Scots Version) Is there for honest Poverty That hings his head, an’ a’ that? The coward-slave, we pass him by, We dare be poor for a’ that! For a’ that, an’ a’ that, Our toils obscure, an’ a’ that, The rank is but the guinea’s stamp, The man’s the gowd for a’ that. What though on hamely fare we dine, Wear hoddin grey, an’ a’ that? Gie fools their silks, and knaves their wine, A man’s a man for a’ that: For a’ that, an’ a’ that, Their tinsel show, an’ a’ that; The honest man, though e’er sae poor, Is king o’ men for a’ that. Ye see yon birkie, ca’d a lord, Wha struts, an’ stares, an’ a’ that; Though hundreds worship at his word, He’s but a coof for a’ that: For a’ that, an’ a’ that, His ribband, star, an’ a’ that, The man o’ independent mind, He looks an’ laughs at a’ that. Then let us pray that come it may, (As come it will for a’ that,) That Sense and Worth, o’er a’ the earth, Shall bear the gree, an’ a’ that. For a’ that, an’ a’ that, It’s coming yet for a’ that, That man to man, the warld o’er, Shall brothers be for a’ that.  @bananasutra lyrics adaptation:  Is there a man who walks with pride, Though poor and worn, and all that? The coward bows, but we’ll abide, We dare be free for all that. For all that and all that, Our toil and sweat and all that, The crown is but a stamped disguise, A man’s a man for all that. What if our table’s plain and bare, Our coats are thin, and all that? Let fools delight in silks so rare, A man’s a man for all that. For all that and all that, Their pomp and gold and all that, An honest heart and mind so free, Are worth far more than all that. You see that man they call a lord, Who struts and stares and all that? Though many bow before his word, He’s but a fool for all that. For all that and all that, His stars and stripes and all that, A man who stands with mind unchained, He laughs and walks past all that. So let us hope the day will come, (And come it will, for all that,) When sense and worth, not birth and gold, Shall lead the world, and all that. For all that and all that, It’s coming yet, for all that, That man to man, both far and wide, Shall brothers be for all that.

description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue. [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue. description: This one started with Tom Waits, saying "There's no Prayer Like Desire".   And then, I thought...  "Truth is NOT found in WHO powers the light, not who we know or like, who won the fight, it’s not about who is good looking, sweet talking, crowd pleasing, or even award winning… truth is WHO about we believe in. Truth is NOT about WHAT we happen to believe in… truth is not what the preachers, saints, or sinners may say, whisper or scream. It’s not what we do that matters, truth is not about what book we choose to read into, it’s what songs we like to sing, or what tales we like share, or what false promises make us linger. Truth is not HOW or WHEN or WHERE we like to dance. It’s not about HOW one delivers an act of faith between two breaths, it’s now HOW others translate where it came from, when they can even fathom, it’s not about where the will to trust old words wisdom leads us, not how we preach along Leviticus or even Confucius. The truth that matters, the only truth I care about is WHY. It is the truth that never lies, because it lies deep inside one’s heart desires. It is why we choose to join the dance, why we break into a trance, why we find balance, why we care to dare bare the lore of lies untold. Truth is the soul that fuels the bold, the brave, it is the fire that burns in one’s true heart’s desire, the only prayer that shines like it’s divine. Truth is the beat of intimate intentions, the pulse of our deepest motivations, the seed of true  salvation. The truth is the only truth that matters is raw, it’s the reason WHY we love to share, WHY we dare to be in the bare, WHY we hope to win, why we pray we live. Because there’s no prayer like desire."  And then, I wrote several short (unreleased) KNOWsutra But(t) Why songs, all titled "There's No Prayer Like Desire"... this is one 'em.  @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [verse 1] Not who powers the light, Not who wins the fight, It’s the song in the air, And the love that we dare.  [verse 2] Truth lies in the why, In the tears when we cry, Not what we preach or believe, But what we feel and receive.  [chorus] There’s no prayer like desire, It’s what lights the fire, It’s not the book we read, But the hunger that we feed.

description: New year, new song, and only two things, darling: get the facts right, keep love in sight, et voilà <3  "Two Things, Darling" is a KNOWsutra EPx11 flows LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES... The song inspired by my all-time fav dead-daddy, the one and only Bertrand Russel, who taught me the conquest happiness is a simple game of curiosity and kindness—for example, when he was asked to outline the advice he would give to future generations, circa 1959:   “I should like to say two things, one intellectual and one moral.  The intellectual thing I should want to say to them is this: When you are studying any matter or considering any philosophy, ask yourself only what are the facts and what is the truth that the facts bear out. Never let yourself be diverted either by what you wish to believe, or by what you think would have beneficent social effects if it were believed. But look only, and solely, at what are the facts.  The moral thing I should wish to say to them is very simple. I should say love is wise, hatred is foolish. In this world, which is getting more and more interconnected, we have to learn to tolerate each other, we have to learn to put up with the fact that some people say things that we don’t like. We can only live together in that way. And if we are to live together and not die together, we should learn the kind of tolerance which is absolutely vital to the continuation of human life on this planet.”  -- @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro] Not a guru, not a god, just a friendly lill’ line, Just Bertrand, my wise old crush, tapping my mind Says the world is small and the future is near And it only takes two things to save us dear  [Verse 1 (the intellectual thing)] Look at the world with unclouded eyes Not what you wish for, not pretty lies Not what feels good, not what sells or saves Just what is true in the light of the day Let the facts be strange, let them be kind Let them humble your heart and sharpen your mind  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Verse 2 (the moral thing)] This world is crowded and beautifully odd Full of people you’ll never fully applaud Some will annoy you, some will offend But none of us make it alone in the end Love isn’t weak and it isn’t naive It’s the only way any of us get to breathe  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Bridge  (true story)] We’re riding one planet through infinite space No spare, no backup, no second place So hold your beliefs with a little bit loose And hold on to each other like it really matters, because, it does  [Final Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Outro (when knowsutra slide into growsutra and glowsutra)] If we’re gonna live, we live this way With honest eyes, please don’t look away Cherish the things that sing like a prayer Let’s dare to share just how much we care  🕊️❤️‍🔥

tags: Jazz & Blues,gipsy jazz,psychedelic cabaret,acoustic poetry,vocal blues,female tenor,smoky,bluesy,dubby,Indie,authenticity,surreal reality
description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Verse 2] To want a name is not enough, To love your life, breathe in the rough. It can’t be faked, to live the beat, Taste the rhythm, embrace the sweet.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Bridge] Why claim titles, rather than dance? Seek magic truths, imagine chance… Each breath’s a rhyme, each stumble, art, Nurture ‘em sparkles in your heart.  [Outro] Be the poem, feel its grace, Explore shadows, shine in space, Forget titles, laughing at thrones… Blessed be the song in our bones.  — Still reading? Yay. You may also like the sister song I released as a single about a year ago: "She Wears the Words  • JAZZsutra Mighty Poetry Minute" ❤️‍🔥

track title: [04] The Fire We Share • There's No Prayer Like Desire • KNOWsutra But(t) Why Accordion Chanson BURLESQUE
ep_title: There's No Prayer Like Desire • KNOWsutra But(t) Why EPx4
description: This one started with Tom Waits, saying "There's no Prayer Like Desire".   And then, I thought...  "Truth is NOT found in WHO powers the light, not who we know or like, who won the fight, it’s not about who is good looking, sweet talking, crowd pleasing, or even award winning… truth is WHO about we believe in. Truth is NOT about WHAT we happen to believe in… truth is not what the preachers, saints, or sinners may say, whisper or scream. It’s not what we do that matters, truth is not about what book we choose to read into, it’s what songs we like to sing, or what tales we like share, or what false promises make us linger. Truth is not HOW or WHEN or WHERE we like to dance. It’s not about HOW one delivers an act of faith between two breaths, it’s now HOW others translate where it came from, when they can even fathom, it’s not about where the will to trust old words wisdom leads us, not how we preach along Leviticus or even Confucius. The truth that matters, the only truth I care about is WHY. It is the truth that never lies, because it lies deep inside one’s heart desires. It is why we choose to join the dance, why we break into a trance, why we find balance, why we care to dare bare the lore of lies untold. Truth is the soul that fuels the bold, the brave, it is the fire that burns in one’s true heart’s desire, the only prayer that shines like it’s divine. Truth is the beat of intimate intentions, the pulse of our deepest motivations, the seed of true  salvation. The truth is the only truth that matters is raw, it’s the reason WHY we love to share, WHY we dare to be in the bare, WHY we hope to win, why we pray we live. Because there’s no prayer like desire."  And then, I wrote several short (unreleased) KNOWsutra But(t) Why songs, all titled "There's No Prayer Like Desire"... this is one 'em.  @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [verse 1] Not who powers the light, Not who wins the fight, It’s the song in the air, And the love that we dare.  [verse 2] Truth lies in the why, In the tears when we cry, Not what we preach or believe, But what we feel and receive.  [chorus] There’s no prayer like desire, It’s what lights the fire, It’s not the book we read, But the hunger that we feed.

description: If this song got you shrugging, smirking, or squirming, man, please pause... and tell me why?   🩸🩸🩸  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro]   They say it’s “too much.”   Too bloody.   Too messy.   Too loud.   Too real.   So I ask…  [Verse 1]   Why’s it taboo to talk of blood,   When half the world’s got cycles that flood?   Why’s it shameful to name a cramp,   But not to wave a warlord’s stamp?  Why is “discharge” more feared than lies?   Why do men squirm while a woman dries—   her tears, her womb, her sleepless nights,   while they debate her basic rights?  [Chorus]   Taboo for who?   Who made the rules?   Who taught us shame   in sterile schools?   It ain’t biology that’s the crime—   It’s silence weaponized through time.    Taboo for who?   'Cause I’m not scared—   I’ll sing what’s real   since they don’t dare.  [Verse 2]   Why is menopause met with a shrug,   while old white men get pills to plug   their shriveled pride with pharma might,   but women sweat through silent nights?  Why is "hormonal" used as a slur,   when the whole damn system *depends* on her?   Why don’t they teach us bone will thin?   Why ain’t that in the doc’s quick spin?  Why is a womb a ticking clock   unless it births, then it’s forgot?   Why is my pain dismissed as flair—   while men’s complaints get urgent care?  [Bridge]   It’s not taboo 'cause it’s grotesque,   it’s taboo 'cause it shows who’s next.   It shows resilience, mess, and might—   and that’s what gives the boys a fright.  [Interlude]   Let’s be honest.   It’s not about discomfort.   It’s about control.   And they’re losing it.  [Final Chorus]   Taboo for who?   I call your bluff.   Your squeamish pride?   Ain’t good enough.   This ain’t shame—it’s sacred truth.   It’s guts and fire and ancient proof.  Taboo for who?   I name the cost—   Of every silence   and line we’ve crossed.   So take your fear and go regroup—   the grown-up talk is in this loop.  [Outro]   If it makes you flinch,   it probably matters.

description: In March 2025 (almost a year ago now, and barely 3 months in office), FOTUS funded a federal “anti-Christian bias” surveillance task force, officially encouraging government employees to snitch on colleagues, globally—anonymously and retroactively, reporting alleged "incidents dating back to the previous administration” (gasp). This dystopian Christian state initiative was framed as protecting “religious freedom” (sic), and blatantly non-constitutional, in multiple ways (in breach of 3 constitutional clauses, to be exact).   I wrote this song the week that memo dropped; when it became overwhelmingly clear (to me) that the rule of law no longer applied. At the time tho, to most, it felt like populist antics, grievance politics wrapped in sanctified language, bureaucratized suspicion dressed up as moral defense… While to me, beyond the shadow of a doubt, it meant authoritarianism was officially here. The American Democracy was dead. It was Orwell’s 1984 Ministry of “Religious Feedom” à la Project 2025 deadly Atwood salsa. And I personally felt devastated, because democracy, liberty, equality, and fraternity are beyond precious; fundamental things worth fighting for yesterday.  Nearly a year later, this track feels like a timestamp of doom, an broken alarm… as publicly funded cruelty and lawless injustice continue to spread on the daily, in all impunity, with full “federal immunity” (to quote Steven Miller directly)—through memos, “temporary” task forces, executive orders, whatchamacallits, etc. And yet, guess what? Most people I know STILL think and say I’m overreacting. True story.   To be clear, this song isn’t anti-faith. It’s anti-fear, and anti-denial. It’s about the difference(s) between “freedom of religion” (a constitutional right) and authoritarian surveillance, where anonymous delation is policy, just like in the good old Gestapo daze, you know? I don’t want to say I told ya, but(t) WOW! You gotta wonder, for Christ’s sake, or something? Because, where will we be next year? How long are we (the people) gonna wank with reckoning fantasies? It’s high time for Rebel Romance, goddamn it... description: Because Gladys is my middle name, and "Sonder" is a magic feeling of knowing wonder--when each stranger you see is the main character of their own life, and you are merely an extra in their story... The word was coined by author John Koenig and first appeared in "The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows", a project that creates names for emotions that don't have one  🕳️🐇   Gipsy Burlesque Blues Dream @bananasutra EPx14 #lyrics (variations):  [Intro – Down the Rabbit Dream]  The curtain breathes smoke, the dream’s out of tune, Gladys sings sideways beneath the fool moon. Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise.   Moral of the story: be the great fool worth being 🃏   Fool psychedelick cabaret EPx30 flows ❯ Flamenco Techno INDIE (1-3) ❯ French Tango JAZZ (4-8) ❯ Gipsy Tango BURLESQUE (9-10) ❯ Circus Waltz BURLESQUE (11-16) ❯ Cabaret Swing BURLESQUE (17-18) ❯ Hip Jazz LOFI (19-22) ❯ Hop Pop LOFI (23-25) ❯ Hillbilly Banjo LOFI (26-29) ❯ Americana Banjo BLUES (30)  (Because the emperor deserves a full orchestra;)  @bananasutra #originallyrics  [Verse 1 — The Great Crown] Some tricksters wandered into town, Selling fake emperor’s crowns, Smiling wide with empty hands, Mumbling words none understands.  They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there.  [Verse 2 — The Great Goons] A buffoon tweets from a gilded throne, While loyal goons praise what ain’t shown, They bow and swear, “Oh, it’s divine!” Then clap along in crooked time.  Echoes ring through hollow halls, Truth gets lost beneath applause, Every doubt gets dipped in gold, Every lie gone wild and old.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Verse 3 — Hello Charlie Chaplin] ’Til one small voice broke through the swing, Soft and kind like Chaplin would sing, “This dicktator is a cheat,” And tender hearts skipped a beat.  A whisper cut through all the noise, Simple truth with humble poise, And for a breath the spell grew thin, Like light was finally let in.  [Bridge — Say no to Complicity] What a vast hallucination, Built on fear and fabrication, Pure race, pure flag, pure vanity, A costume stitched in complicity.  Pomposity in rigid seams, An empire built on shattered dreams, Promises broken, dragged along, By silent crowds that make it strong.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Outro — The Fool Worth Being] It’s a foolish thing, absurd to see, But(t) why play along with stupidity? Let’s laugh out loud and break the ring, And be the fool worth being.  — PS: This release also passes the mark of 2K #bananasutra tracks released on SoundCloud since 2024 🍌💨 #WOOT

description: Light me up, librarian lover… and "Read Me Harder" EPX19 📚💨 Side A x9 = Gypsy HopFi Fusion BURLESQUE Edition Side B x10 = Psychedelic Americana BLUES Edition  I was listening to my "S.S. is for Sacred Sp3rm" EP when I saw yet another one of those daily terrifying #breakingnews social media posts, listing #books recently #banned from the (remaining) U.S. Public Schools and Libraries #circa2025  1. The Handmaid’s Tale by Margaret Atwood 2. Brave New World, by Aldous Huxley 3. Fahrenheit 451 by Ray Bradbury 4. 1984 by George Orwell 5. To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee 6. The perks of being a wallflower, by Stephen Chbovsky 7. The Bluest Eye by Toni Morrison  8. Sold by Patricia McCormick 9. Maus by Art Spiegelman 10. An African and Latinx History of the United States by Paul Ortiz  So then, I had to write a "B.B. is for BANNED BOOKS" song, to honor my favorite authors on this list, because WOW... HOW freaking SCARY of an #americanhorror #truestory IS THAT?!   ☆☆☆ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They banned the truth for being rude… But baby, rude is how we bloom. So light me up, librarian lover… and read me harder. B.B. is for Banned Books, and Badass Brains.  [Verse 1 – Harper Lee & Art Spiegelman] Harper told me, “Mock me, kill me,” still I sing, Truth’s a mockingbird with wings. Art drew the pain, a mouse in flame, He said, “Remember, never tame.” You can ban my ink, but not my roar, I’ll scratch your walls, and write some more.  [Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! If thinking’s sin, I’ll take the blame, Desire and truth are one and same.  [Verse 2 – Aldous Huxley & Margaret Atwood] Aldous whispered, “Take your soma, stay asleep,” But sugar, freedom don’t come cheap. Atwood smirked, “Blessed be the fruit,” Then laced her boots and staged a coup. Pop your soma, hush your fear, But holy lust still lights us clear.  [Bridge – George Orwell & Ray Bradbury] Big Brother’s watching, Ray lit the spark, Said, “Burn the dark, not those who mark.” Orwell winked through smoke and steam, “Truth’s a thoughtcrime, love’s the dream.” You can’t delete what won’t forget, We’re the match they can’t reset.  [Final Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! Truth’s taboo, but damn, it’s neat, Come turn the page with me.  [Outro] For Harper Lee, Art Spiegelman, Aldous Huxley, Margaret Atwood, George Orwell, and Ray Bradbury, for every mind they tried to muzzle. We see you. We feel you. And we’ll keep reading you harder.

description: People often ask me how I make songs, and the answer forever is it depends! That is the beauty of practicing the experimental art of creativity, it teaches us the paths to happiness are essentially like imagination, i.e.infinite. All you really need is a brave and open mind, and (more importantly) a curious and gratefool heart...   "Donkeys Years" is a SHOWsutra Fanana Club EP (i.e. where monkeys & donkeys play), because it was inspired by a silly party chit chat that brought me joy in the moment—plus, British humor is deliciously quirky cheeky (like I like), and huh, well, it's true I'm a hardcore slut for new words and expressions lol. But(t)... it is also very much infused with FLOWsutra and GLOWsutra vibes (i.e. where trust & gratitude shine), because at its core, it is (yet another:) thank you letter, to music, friends, fun, and freedom.    EPx20 flows (Side A) Dub INDIE ❯ Gipsy LOFI + (Side B) Fusion JAZZ ❯ Psychedelic BURLESQUE + (BONUS) a Ragga Mama Dub DUB finale, olé 💃🏻  -- @bananasutra  #originalsong #lyrics   🎵 DONKEYS YEARS  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 1] Desert dust and beachside bass, Silly smiles on every face. Trippy souls and jesters peers, Dancing through the donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 2] Forest nights and valley drums, Booty-shaking wisdom comes. Finding freedom, in trance gears, My monkey dears, my donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Glow-Out Outro] Thank you, ravers, light and loud, May we find healing in the crowd. SHOWsutra bows with peace fool grace… Now let’s hug once more,  and meet me by the bass

description: I'm no religion lover... but like all good Christians, I do my best to keep an open heart and flexible perspective (haha). And in that moment I saw Leo (the new American-Peruvian pope) chose to end his first little public statement by #bewoke instead of amen, I felt sooo much relief, I cried in #gratitude 🙏 and then, I was compelled to make a celebratory song or 2 about it hehe   @bananasutra lyrics, with a classic Jazz to Dub to Cello Indie flow :)  I woke up with a holy gasp—on a headline line, “An American Pope?”—sucked like end of time. My coffee froze, my heart beat “nope,” But turns out, Leo just may be dope…  [Chorus] No es Trump, no es loco, Ain’t slingin’ hate or playin’ poco. He prays in Spanish, walks con paz, No holy walls, no holy brass. So yeah, it’s weird, but breathe real slow— El Papa no es gringo malo, bro.  He chilled in Perú, with dust on his shoes, Didn’t roll up in jets, or preached loud fake news. Got MAGA rosaries, no Bible bling, His name’s Leo—not some right-wing king.  Ain’t postin’ prayers on Threads or X, Ain’t blessin’ greed or crypto checks. No evil tweets, no dark grace, No gold-plated lies or metaverse face.  [Chorus] So calm your fears, let rumors go, Seems more mate than MAGA show. Now light a blunt and take it slow— El Papa no es gringo malo, bro.   No panic, today… not this pope. Just fact-checked truths, and a bit of #hope

description: It's Pride month, with a capital P. And truth be told, as queer and principled as I might be, loud and proud was never my thing. Justice gagged, power abused… Just ICE, and I ain’t freakin’ amused.  Clowns turned fashos, high on plastic straws, Con men with small dicks ruling the law…  [Chorus] No spark, just glitter… fake, no halo. Talk loud, sound bitter… ego ain’t your amigo. No heart, no rhythm… lies in the limbo. Bimbos with no flow… ego ain’t your amigo.  Florida bros? Nah, this runs deeper. Island names dropped, old men, grim reapers.. Cameras glitch, and dead witnesses wit, The truth gone drowned, down a dirty martini sip  Murder or myth? Who wrote this script? When ‘em bozos wear suits and the courts just flip… A convicted felon, small screen sensation, Ego playin’ hero, in a faux-blessed nation.  This ain’t satire, mama, It is a dire drama. Greedy egos gone guns, Bad jokes, old puns.  No schools, no rights, Like plight turned blight, Red trucker hats, Eatin’ your cats?!  Oh Ego ain’t your amigo… Please beware of ‘em plastic straws. May we find a muse who plays ‘em heartstrings, Making magic, a song we can sing.  Tell me, is it true? Is it fair? Is it fun? Are we free, or just numb, marchin’ to a drum? If truth is the joke, and the lie is the show, What’s a soul to do but blow, blow, and blow?  [Chorus] No spark, just glitter… fake, no halo. Talk loud, sound bitter… ego ain’t your amigo. No heart, no rhythm… lies in the limbo. Watch close, they slither… ego ain’t your amigo.  Oh hi, oh hey, well hey hey there, hello, This is song for a world gone loco. Sing it loud, and diss the plastic straw, bro… Now you know, ego ain’t your amigo.

track title: [02] The (Bloody Mountain) Echo - Vladimir Vysotsky English Cover - BLOWsutra Gipsy La Poesita Cello Indie Folk DUB
ep_title: The Echo Song Song ☭ Vladimir Vysotsky - EPx6  English Cover ☭ BLOWsutra Gipsy Trip Hop Trip
description: A friend of mine asserted that this song, by Soviet singer-songwriter and poet Vladimir #vysotsky is “a perfect song” (PART 2): so... I first indulged in creating the Russian version (because I have a bit of an accent fetish lol), and now (of course), I had to try the Vladimir Vysotsky "Echo Song" (as I say, in my head, ha) in English too.   This EPx6 flows like Gipsy Dub, Dub, Lofi, Burlesque, Indie, Indie Gipsy 🌬️🗿🎶  Note: this is a rare @banananustra cover (i.e. not an original song), and my only cover of a song not in #publicdomain  Credits: poetic Soviet Singer-Songwriter Vladimir Vysotsky #lyrics translation by Vagalec (slightly edited)  ☭ ☭ ☭  The (Bloody Mountain) Mountain Echo   In a mountain pass, where the rocks for the winds are no checkers (no checkers), Where no one has ever set foot, so steep is the rise (so steep is the rise), There once lived a jubilant, cheerful mountain echo, It answered all calls, and replied to the cries, human cries.  When loneliness suddenly fills our heart with despair (with despair), And when a low sound of pain down the cliff starts to land (starts to land), The echo, adroitly, will pick up the call,And handling with care, Will lift it, and louder, with tenderness take it in hand.  But some scoundrels, madmen and drunkards, got round (got round), So that no one might hear the footfall and snort (footfall and snort), Intending to silence and murder the gorge, living canyon They bound up the echo, and stopped up its mouth ere they shot.  And so it went on, their bloody, ferocious, enraged merrymaking  No sound could be heard as they trampled the echo, made fun of it, mocked... They shot, in the morning, the quieted mountain echo (mountain echo) And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock... And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock... And tears gushed out like stones from the wounds of the rock...

description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... Blessed be the sound in our bones ✨  EPx16 flow: ❯ Sultry JAZZ (1-2) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (3-5) ❯ Dreamy DUB (6-10) ❯ Indie BURLESQUE (11-14) ❯ Smoky BLUES (15-16)  — @bananasutra “Kiss a Pulse” #songwriter #lyrics  [Verse 1] So many dream of poet’s fame, Celebrate names like some lame game, Wearing words like ego prizes… But joy is awe, not disguises.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Verse 2] To want a name is not enough, To love your life, breathe in the rough. It can’t be faked, to live the beat, Taste the rhythm, embrace the sweet.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Bridge] Why claim titles, rather than dance? Seek magic truths, imagine chance… Each breath’s a rhyme, each stumble, art, Nurture ‘em sparkles in your heart.  [Outro] Be the poem, feel its grace, Explore shadows, shine in space, Forget titles, laughing at thrones… Blessed be the song in our bones.  — Still reading? Yay. description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... Blessed be the sound in our bones ✨  EPx16 flow: ❯ Sultry JAZZ (1-2) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (3-5) ❯ Dreamy DUB (6-10) ❯ Indie BURLESQUE (11-14) ❯ Smoky BLUES (15-16)  — @bananasutra “Kiss a Pulse” #songwriter #lyrics  [Verse 1] So many dream of poet’s fame, Celebrate names like some lame game, Wearing words like ego prizes… But joy is awe, not disguises.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Verse 2] To want a name is not enough, To love your life, breathe in the rough. It can’t be faked, to live the beat, Taste the rhythm, embrace the sweet.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Bridge] Why claim titles, rather than dance? Seek magic truths, imagine chance… Each breath’s a rhyme, each stumble, art, Nurture ‘em sparkles in your heart.  [Outro] Be the poem, feel its grace, Explore shadows, shine in space, Forget titles, laughing at thrones… Blessed be the song in our bones.  — Still reading? Yay. You may also like the sister song I released as a single about a year ago: "She Wears the Words  • JAZZsutra Mighty Poetry Minute" ❤️‍🔥

description: “But(t) How Can You?” is a silly quirky GROWsutra (i.e. where we be brave) detective story chasing conscience. Think Velma and Scooby-Doo gone "Where Are You!", but(t) asking philosophical questions that matter, instead of hunting ghosts with banter (same same, lol).  Blessed with goofy curiosity, a raised eyebrow, and magick howling glasses, they wonder how people manage to ignore the monsters—when science, education, and justice are getting booed by stinky fascist poo... How can one witness obvious, nefarious, scary dystopian  authoritarian nonsense, and just shrug?!  Across ragga DUB (1-4), gypsy LOFI (5-8), and INDIE cello sighs (8-9), this EPx10 pokes at cowardice and denial, and sings the clues of a simple mystery: what happens when good conscience meets convenient silence? Spoiler: Scooby knows something smells funny, woo, but(t) also boo 👻  — @bananasutra #lyrics   Well, have you met your good conscience, Or you buried it in silence? Well, have you heard of what’s science, Or you deny it in essence? I’m just saying ‘cause I’m curious, And education is glorious.  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!  Well now, who’s gonna take a chance, At true leadership, present tense? I’m just singing ‘cause I’m nervous, And I wish we’d be more cautious…  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!

description: “I didn’t mind zero orgasm. But(t) zero empathy is goddamn shitty. I didn’t mind the finite chasm. But(t) zero sum is so darn petty.”  An experimental post-punk gipsy dub cabaret autopsy of a finite petty game played by a wannabe punk with nothing but(t) junk. Inspired by Grace Hopper’s first actual case of bug being found—because some bugs aren’t found in code but(t) in character.  Bug found: NO EMPATHY. Infinite test result: FAILED. Diagnostic: BUGS GOT NO GRACE. Features: Camus, Russell, Brel, one absurdist fart, and the subjective finite game theory of a wannabe punk who chose selfishness over connectedness, defect over respect, and contempt over content. track title: [11] Hello, Oh No • GROWsutra Psychedelic Queen of Authentic Dubby Folk Banjo BLUES
ep_title: Hello · Oh No • EPx16 • GROWsutra Psychedelic Logic Harmonics
tags: Conscious music,Folk & Singer-Songwriter,psychedelic poetry,soul fool,social commentary,ethical leadership,lo-fi fusion,alternative folk,trippy acoustic,cheeky philosophy,wink in the dark,Religion & Spirituality,News & Politics
description: “Hello, Oh No?” is a silly, cheeky GROWsutra true story that sings like psychedelic poetry, a hope-fool tune asking simple questions that actually matter, in a world gone mad bananas, a world that forgot how cute it is to blush... Think of it as a friendly wink in the dark, a small song with big questions—playful on the surface, philosophical underneath.  It’s about the magic healing power of free will, the importance of critical thinking with a pulse. It’s about courage, honesty, humility, and unity, i.e. the superpowers we misplaced somewhere on the cha-ching media conveyor belt, where noise dressed up as wisdom, and ego bought a throne and called it strength—because really, who(tf) sold us the myth that success means crushing others, and fear beats love? And why(tf) did we applaud?!  I wrote this for the brave dreamers and future-makers, to dare you to care for the kids and the grown-ups who got bamboozled along the way; the ones who were told empathy was weak and win-win was naïve, while hollow peacocks in blinged-out power suits paraded around calling hoarding “leadership.” Even though history keeps whispering the same truth: it is kindness that defines real winners.  This song hums a gentle but stubborn reminder: real winners don’t blindfold themselves for comfort. They choose spark over dark. Win-win over win-lose that end up being lose-lose. Empathy over hypocrisy. Unity over vanity. Because, see... kindness isn’t weakness, it’s clarity. Win-win isn’t cute or “woke”, it’s pragamatic, it's empiric, it's strategic. And humility? Oh darling, that’s DIVINE!  And maybe, just maybe, if we stop mistaking leadership for expensive cosplay, and start choosing clearer hearts over louder heroes, maybe we’ll see through the toxic smoke of shiny mirrors? Maybe we’ll recognize ego-madness when it struts by, cocky dressed as fancy progress. Maybe we’ll even learn (or remember) to laugh at (not with) the pompous Prometheus and snake oil fraudsters,  selling cha-ching over win-win sharing… Maybe. Can we?  So now, hello, oh no?!… What will you choose, bro? The choice is (y)ours.  EPx16 flows  ❯ Dreamy DUB (1-3) ❯ Ragga DUB (4) ❯ Flamenco DUB (5-6) ❯ Fusion LoFi (7-8) ❯ Tango JAZZ (9) ❯ Gipsy JAZZ (10)  ❯ Psychedelic BLUES (11-12) ❯ Bluegrass BANJO (13-14) ❯ Post-Punk BURLESQUE (15-16)  (because diversity matters ;)  — @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1] Hello, oh no! description: “No Fear, My Dear” is a new bluesy humanist piano jazz kinda psychedelic soul torch song EPx19—a love letter inspired by and dedicated to the one and only Nina Simone, all strong women, and to the simple, not-so-radical idea that freedom only begins when fear ends 🕊️  EPx19 is a no BS BLOWsutra (Revolt Now) meditation, an agnostic prayer hour for truth, justice, & solidarity (for a world gone mad bananas)... yet another empathetic and courageous pep talk of light for dark times, to help our guts know, our hope grow, and our hearts glow  ❤️‍🔥  Side A (1-10) honors Nina's love for timeless acoustic bluesy piano jazz magic 🪄 Side B (11-19) indulges my love for psychedelic dub + indie folk + banjo blues + gipsy lofi experimental genres fusion  🏴‍☠️  ❢ ❢ ❢  @bananasutra song #lyrics   [INTRO] “I’ll tell you what freedom means to me… No fear, my dear, freedom means no fear.” And if my voice should tremble, Let it ring loud and clear.  [VERSE 1 — “I Had a Dream”] I had a dream we woke as one, No hearts undone, no souls outrun. A world where truths walked side by side, And no one had to run or hide.  [VERSE 2 — Strong-Women] My mother said, “Stand tall, my girl, Don’t bend your fire to fit their world.” She taught me souls can crack and break, But dignity’s our own to make.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [VERSE 3 — Sound-as-Salvation] Some pray in halls of dust and stone, Some kneel where tired saints have gone. But I find truth in rhythm’s rise, Where basslines pull the dark to light.  [VERSE 4 — Mirror of the Times] We watch the days grow mean and cold, Let’s join our hands, and break that mold. Let artists shine where lies appear, Hold a mirror against the fear.  [BRIDGE] If sorrow’s got you by the throat, I’ve walked that road, I know that note. Storm winds can strip us to the bone, And still we rise, don’t feel alone.  They’ll call the truth a threat, a scar, They’ll twist the past to dim a star. But breathe, my love, hold your own mark. Let freedom burn their toxic snark.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [OUTRO] If your voice should tremble, Let it tremble to the light. No fear, my dear, Let’s sing it through the night…  ❢ ❢ ❢

track title: [02] Le Bal Des Salauds • French BLOWsutra Gipsy LoFi Chanson INDIE
ep_title: Le Bal Des Salauds - French BLOWsutra Indie Gipsy Burlesque EPx9
description: Ce qui est marrant c'est que salaud au féminin, en français, c'est pas salaude! Ha, #justsayin Chanson inspirée par un vrai livre recent intitulé "Le Temp Des Salauds" 🍟🤓🤌  @bananasutra lyrics (variantions):  [Intro] Bienvenue, mesdames et messieurs,  Au grand bal des vertus douteuses.  Ici, les salauds dansent heureux,  Les cœurs vendus, les mains soyeuses.  Leur morale est bien repassée,  Mais toujours un peu tachée.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds, Des faux héros, des pantins d’ego,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  C’est le temps des salauds, oh-oh,  Des beaux parleurs, des faux normaux,  Qui rient très haut… pour mentir plus beau.  [Couplet 1 – Le délire raisonnable] Le nouveau réalisme, c’est l’art des salauds,  Un délirium sobre, cynisme en costard chaud.  Ils vendent la peur sous cellophane,  Et t’appellent “extrême” si tu dis “humain”.  Ils posent des questions de sages,  Mais répondent comme des mirages sauvages.  Ils jouent à la raison...  mais raisonnent faux,  C’est la saison, la moisson des salauds.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des cerveaux trop clos,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  [Couplet 2 – Les alliances du vide] Trois types de salauds, faut l’dire clair:  Les politiques, les patrons, les faiseurs d’prières.  Ceux qui savent mais trahissent,  Eux les lâches, qui profitent.  Le p’tit Jupiter, Machiavel au moral,  Fait valser les foules dans son bal libéral.  Il pactise, il nuance, tord le vrai,  Pour qu’le faux paraisse sensé.  [Pont] Forts avec les faibles, faibles avec les forts,  Ils vendent la paix pendant qu’ils signent la mort.  “Bon courage”, qu’ils disent, le sourire faux,  Mais c’est un orage… on danse, salauds?  [Couplet 3 – Les fous et les faux] Les fous aboient, les salauds cadrent,  Et les cons signent tous les contrats.  Les uns hurlent, les autres calculent,  Et les lucides… se taisent, s’annulent.  Les idoles changent, les valeurs se vendent,  La foule like, la vérité s’attend.  Les héros sont devenus salauds,  Nous, figurants d’un online show.  [Refrain – Final] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des gros egos,  Qui valsent au rythme des fiascos,  Au bal, au bal des salauds! (oh-oh)  Au bal… des salauds.  [Outro] J’en ai aimé, des salauds, c’est vrai,  Leurs mots brillants, leurs airs parfaits.  Mais minuit sonne, le bal s’oublie,  Ces salauds-là ne dansent plus… avec ma vie.

description: “This Is My Quest” is a sincere GROWsutra (Dare to Care) prayer song inspired by one of my all time favorite French song, Jacques Brel’s “La Quête”. description: … a solemn, tragic poem made of tears turned into a song⸻in the name of the sacred democratic truth, for the many wounded already, and the millions yet to be wronged, ignored or terrorized, hunted, jailed, starved, and enslaved... all silenced by American fasc!sts  ☠ ☆☆☆   @bananasutra lyrics:  ⸻ I speak not for power, nor pride in disguise, But for the Earth, for the children with frightened eyes. For the silence that screamed when no one replied, For the truth that you buried, and the books you denied.  For the mothers unheard, for the breath that was choked, For the treaties you tore, for the bridges you broke. I come not with fury, but with memory’s flame— To whisper the names that you covered in shame.  ⸻ [Chorus] Hereby I cry, in the name of the still, Of the sacred, the silenced, the hearts you won’t kill. Not to punish, not to preach, not to tear down the sky— Just to speak what was true. Hereby, I cry.  ⸻ You crowned the cruel, gave the false your stage, Called it “truth” when it trembled, “strength” when it raged. You sold off the soil, made a brand of belief, Preached “freedom” while peddling despair and deceit.  You mocked the meek, turned mercy to sin, Put pride in a costume and fear in its grin. But I come not to damn — just to testify, That love was still here. Hereby, I cry.  ⸻ You crowned a man who mocked the scar, Whose name sits in courtrooms, yet shines like a star. You laughed with him — while others bled, Called truth “too woke,” and justice “dead.”  He joked of touch like it was game, While survivors bore the weight and shame. But silence is not peace — it’s the cost we deny. So in their name, Hereby, I cry.  ⸻ If decency paid like fame and spin, He’d be the poorest man to ever win. Bankrupt in soul, in truth, in grace — But rich in smirks and courtroom face.  No vault could hold the debt he owes — To women, to children, to winds that know. If justice kept ledgers, if conscience could bill, He’d owe the Earth a mountain still.  ⸻ So if you hear this, may you hold it true — Not just for me, but for what we undo. For every child still learning the cost, Of a world that forgets who and what it lost.  Hereby, I cry.

description: “Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers—Build your hope on reason’s stairs.”  I love this song very much, and am overdue to share it :) It was inspired by a bold and brilliant essay Bertrand Russell wrote in 1929 (and for fool disclosure, Bertrand is my all-time favorite philosopher, and was also a renowned mathematician; if you're curious, I recommend you check out "The Conquest of Happiness"). His essay aims to answer a question I've asked myself for as long as I can remember, an important one: “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”   His answer? Not really—and certainly not uniquely.... long story short, here's what he concludes: * Compassion doesn’t require dogma. * Progress thrives on questions, not creeds. * Morality rooted in obedience is not morality—it’s fear in disguise.  He believed humanity could find meaning, ethics, and joy through reason, science, and humanism—no gods or thrones required. This song echoes that spirit: a love letter to curiosity, courage, and clarity. A little irreverent, a lot sincere.  --- @bananasutra “Reason Over Reverence” fool lyrics ✨  They built the heavens with fear in the sky, Promised salvation but told us to die. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  No eternal fire, no thrones on high, Just the vast unknown where truths collide. We walk the earth with curious eyes, Finding meaning where wonder lies.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  So let’s build a world where all can explore, Free from the chains of the dogma of yore. For in the search, not the faith, we’ll find, The beauty of life and the power of mind.  ⭐︎⭐︎⭐︎

Elon’s success, for example, only proves he’s a coucou twat… A nasty bird defined by cocksure opportunism (like his current boss), who chased fame and wealth motivated by pathological desires of proving his criminal father wrong, and delusional fantasies of world domination. Dolon Trusk is not a “smart” guy here to save planet earth from gas emissions,Nah! So, what I’m saying is take care of your soul, dear. Please beware of ignorance, call out malevolence, their shallow truths are cold, dark, and toxic thoughts—or you’ll never, GROW, flow, GLOW, and BOW… This is what the songs of the bananasutra bible are all about—to help us remember what actually matters, to be safe and happy together 🍌💨  —  Original bananasutra song inspired by the poem “Kindness”—Naomi Shihab Nye (1952). Here’s the original poem:  Before you know what kindness really is you must lose things, feel the future dissolve in a moment like salt in a weakened broth. What you held in your hand, what you counted and carefully saved, all this must go so you know how desolate the landscape can be between the regions of kindness. How you ride and ride thinking the bus will never stop, the passengers eating maize and chicken will stare out the window forever.  Before you learn the tender gravity of kindness you must travel where the Indian in a white poncho lies dead by the side of the road. You must see how this could be you, how he too was someone who journeyed through the night with plans and the simple breath that kept him alive. ​ Before you know kindness as the deepest thing inside, you must know sorrow as the other deepest thing. You must wake up with sorrow. You must speak to it till your voice catches the thread of all sorrows and you see the size of the cloth. Then it is only kindness that makes sense anymore, only kindness that ties your shoes and sends you out into the day to gaze at bread, only kindness that raises its head from the crowd of the world to say It is I you have been looking for, and then goes with you everywhere like a shadow or a friend. description: “Hello, Oh No?” is a silly, cheeky GROWsutra true story that sings like psychedelic poetry, a hope-fool tune asking simple questions that actually matter, in a world gone mad bananas, a world that forgot how cute it is to blush... Think of it as a friendly wink in the dark, a small song with big questions—playful on the surface, philosophical underneath.  It’s about the magic healing power of free will, the importance of critical thinking with a pulse. It’s about courage, honesty, humility, and unity, i.e. the superpowers we misplaced somewhere on the cha-ching media conveyor belt, where noise dressed up as wisdom, and ego bought a throne and called it strength—because really, who(tf) sold us the myth that success means crushing others, and fear beats love? And why(tf) did we applaud?!  I wrote this for the brave dreamers and future-makers, to dare you to care for the kids and the grown-ups who got bamboozled along the way; the ones who were told empathy was weak and win-win was naïve, while hollow peacocks in blinged-out power suits paraded around calling hoarding “leadership.” Even though history keeps whispering the same truth: it is kindness that defines real winners.  This song hums a gentle but stubborn reminder: real winners don’t blindfold themselves for comfort. They choose spark over dark. Win-win over win-lose that end up being lose-lose. Empathy over hypocrisy. Unity over vanity. Because, see... kindness isn’t weakness, it’s clarity. Win-win isn’t cute or “woke”, it’s pragamatic, it's empiric, it's strategic. And humility? Oh darling, that’s DIVINE!  And maybe, just maybe, if we stop mistaking leadership for expensive cosplay, and start choosing clearer hearts over louder heroes, maybe we’ll see through the toxic smoke of shiny mirrors? Maybe we’ll recognize ego-madness when it struts by, cocky dressed as fancy progress. Maybe we’ll even learn (or remember) to laugh at (not with) the pompous Prometheus and snake oil fraudsters,  selling cha-ching over win-win sharing… Maybe. Can we?  So now, hello, oh no?!… What will you choose, bro? The choice is (y)ours. What’s the deal? Do we fight, or do we heal? To shine, or whine, it’s your choice, Kindness always lifts your voice.  Loving, not just winning, true, Don’t play the game to make others blue. Silly or nasty, the choice is clear, A little love wipes away the fear.  [Chorus] Hello, oh no! What do you choose? A spark or dark, which will you use? To win with love, that’s how we fly, Bye-bye, boo, no need to cry!  [Verse 2] Be true or be fake, it’s up to you, Will you share, or be a gangster too? Ha ha, boo ya, which will it be? There’s magic in humility.  Encore, the lore, let’s dance some more, A win-win’s waiting at the door. Be kind, not blind, and you’ll see, The real win’s in harmony.  [Chorus] Hello, oh no! What do you choose? A spark or dark, which will you use? To win with love, that’s how we fly, Bye-bye, boo, no need to cry!  [Bridge] A spark shines bright, the night turns day, When we choose love, the darkness fades away. Cha-ching or win-win, what do you see? The real prize lies in unity.  [Outro] Hello, oh no! We all can win, Let love lead, let’s begin again!

description: How do you feel about financing neofascism, Murica? Are you feeling dangerously insane yet? I'm asking because, to be completely honest, I dunno what(tf) dissent looks like now—but(t) I'm thinking not paying federal taxes seems like a reasonable, effective way to RESIST authoritarian cruelty, for example. I also desperately wonder why so few are reacting, much less organizing. Why are elected representatives doing what seems to account to basically nothing? Where(tf) are the brave thinkers, the benevolent leaders, the new millennium's progressive Joan of Arc? HOW CAN I HELP?   I dunno, but(t) I dare ask... even with just another BLOWsutra Revolution Ring song of yesterdays and tomorrows gone banana—it’s raw, it’s flawed, bloody dirty goddamn heck, it’s Monday in Murica 🙈🙉🙊🍟   — [Intro] No, it’s not bullshit as usual... The new normal is not neutral. Consent’s just gone, Rights abandoned. Democracy’s dead, Dissent’s gone dread...  [Verse 1 – state surveillance & corporate control] We used to scream into the streets, Now silence starts inside our feeds. They call it bugs… but posts go poof! YouTube’s chat rewrites the truth.  It’s a game of men of shame, History’s a threat to them. Big Tech broke its poker face, Now every scroll’s a hiding place.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: Invisible, internal, thin, A muted thought beneath your skin. It’s algorithms, not a gun, But hun, that’s how new wars are won. This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 2 – systemic institutional sabotage] They gutted justice from its core, Civil servants walked out the door. Philosophy? Deleted. Gone… Because ideas might catch on!  The deans stay quiet, donors cheer. The law’s sold in the name of fear. A government of grift and dare, Where treason hides in legal wear.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: A clause erased, a mail delayed, A syllabus they never made, A lawyer’s oath that’s lost its weight, A student debt that seals a fate… This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 3 – engineered chaos & bots Control] They seed the feeds with farmed out bots, Praise God, and peddle prison plots. The “debates” are traps that loop and stall, Just rage machines to waste us all.  Your logic’s flagged, your truth’s dismissed, While trolls define who can exist. They shoot and fire, then say “calm down”, And blame the victim, as most yawn...  [Bridge – this is not a drill] It’s not a glitch, It’s not a test, It’s policy, A bloody mess!  They want confusion, Promote delusion. They bait with faith, Then fear, then wrath!  Every move is built to break, Not fix, Not free, Not heal, Just take!  [Verse 4 – NO ONE IS SAFE] No trial, no truth, no public proof, No prayer strong enough to soothe. Deport the loud, imprison the poor, Fund new cages, then build some more!  Speak the truth and lose your claim. No jobs, no aids, hopes gone in flame. Their plan is prepped, the script’s in place, And it’s ruthless, death wears no face…  [Final Chorus – the end game, i.e. so what now?] This is what dissent looks like now: A lullaby beneath a drone, A name redacted from a phone, A felon tweeting from hell’s throne.  May we dare scream, cry out loud… This is what dissent looks like now? 🕊️🩸

description: This EPx8 is a compilation of old but(t) not forgotten dystopian Americana songs in my BLOWsutra backlog, and part of the MAxA Series.   It's written as an ABC and titled MAMA, because it's dedicated to the kids, the innocents, the future, here and abroad; to the millions who do and will suffer or die unnecessarily, as a direct result of authoritarian ignorance, powered by ego, greed, and cruelty in a world gone freaking fasci!st bananas AGAIN!   It's also a personal meditation (rumination?;) on leaving Murica for good, and go back to France... It's raw, it's real, it's messy, it's scary, it's heartbreaking, really 🍌♾️  -- @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics (variations):  M-A-G-A Was that a spell or a scam? You meant Make America Great Again?  Funny.  It sounds more like Make America… MINE.  Mama?  Yeah… that tracks.  Make America Mine, Achtung,  Like a toddler in a war room,  Like a Junior with no hug,  Like a grown-ass boy with nukes and mommy issues...  MAMA, Make America Mine Achtung.  Say it louder… but only in English. ( Unless you’re South African and white, then come on in.)  You call it freedom,  But it feels like fear.  You call it order,  But all I see is ruin.  MACA, Make America Christian Again.  But not the poor man’s Christ.  No, the white one,  The one with stock options and a private jet.  MADA, Make America Dumb Again.  Ban the books, burn the facts, shut the libraries.  But hey, Bible apps come pre-installed.  MADA, Make America Disabled Again.  No healthcare, No net,  Can’t walk? Can’t pay?  Can’t matter.  MADA (again), Make America Delusional Again.  Who needs truth… when you’ve got vibes?  Who needs votes… When you’ve got merch?  You call it freedom, But it feels like fear.  You call it order, But all I see is ruin.  MAFA, Make America Felons Again.  Insider trades, Wall Street saints,  But God help the kid  Selling water on the corner  MAHA, Make America Hell Again.  Hunger. Hate. Hysteria.  Wrapped in a smile,  A cross, And a flag pin.  MALA, Make America Loot Again.  Loot the Constitution… loot the consent.  Felons in office,  Children in cages.  You promised greatness.  But you delivered grift. You promised freedom.  But gave us fear.   And more prisons after the mass deportations. For who, exactly? The math don’t add up.  The soul don’t either.  Who wins in this America?  Who’s safer?  Who’s richer?  Who’s freer?  MANA, Make America Nazi Again.  Deport the birthright.  Turn ICE into shadows.  Call that... order.  MAPA, Make America Poor Again.  Cut the wages, raise the rent, kill the food stamps.  Hungry kids?  Too bad! we got deportation budgets to feed.  MARA, Make America Racist Again.  Confederate flags in the halls of Congress.  Ban Black history,  Claim “colorblind”,  But only white walks free.  MAVA, Make America Violent Again.  More cops, less care. More jails, fewer jobs.  “Protect and serve”?  Nah… Just patrol and purge.  [Outro] All I see… is ruin.  And no one’s even asking: Why rule a country you’ve set on fire? Unless… That was the plan all along. M-A-G-A Was never a promise. It was a threat.  And maybe the only thing great that’s coming is a plane ticket home...   🧢🍟

description: This one happened really fast, with Morissey—I mean, the song, start to finish, it’s inspired from #Some girls are bigger than others”, I like the light sense of double entendre, it’s like a subtle dirty banana joke (lol) 🍌❤️‍🔥  [Intro / Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies dig holes in tomorrows, Trolling low like cheap rerun shows. [Verse 2] We’re tied to tricks, sugared illusion, Sweet-spoken chains of confusion, Truth tastes too sharp on dulled out tongues, As crooks howl along their harrowed songs.  [Pre-Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, The longer the lies, the deeper we follow, Down echo roads where hopes lie hollow.  [Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies grow roots in tomorrows, Digging graves with faith gone hollow.
