[Break - soft, intimate] It isn’t fair… Hopes still matter. It ain’t weakness… Truth is progress.  [Final Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies drown my trust in tomorrows, Sealing fates hollowed by ego bros…  [Outro] But I’d rather choke on honest air, Than swallow seas that sink what’s fair, Or breathe ‘em lies like chosen prayers… Blessed be rivers of brave thinkers.

description: Every ​⁠@bananasutra song is a humble pep talk (at least to myself), an agnostic prayer of sorts—this one is one of my fav (hence the Vol. 03:), it was inspired by #leonardcohen #peace #poetry minus #theirony (bc I’m nowhere as deep and subtle as Leonard ;)  ✔✔✔  “Everybody Knows” Gipsy Trip Hop EPx7 #lyrics  [Verse 1] Can we forget the foolishness, just for tonight? description: New year, new song, and only two things, darling: get the facts right, keep love in sight, et voilà <3  "Two Things, Darling" is a KNOWsutra EPx11 flows LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES... The song inspired by my all-time fav dead-daddy, the one and only Bertrand Russel, who taught me the conquest happiness is a simple game of curiosity and kindness—for example, when he was asked to outline the advice he would give to future generations, circa 1959:   “I should like to say two things, one intellectual and one moral.  The intellectual thing I should want to say to them is this: When you are studying any matter or considering any philosophy, ask yourself only what are the facts and what is the truth that the facts bear out. Never let yourself be diverted either by what you wish to believe, or by what you think would have beneficent social effects if it were believed. But look only, and solely, at what are the facts.  The moral thing I should wish to say to them is very simple. I should say love is wise, hatred is foolish. In this world, which is getting more and more interconnected, we have to learn to tolerate each other, we have to learn to put up with the fact that some people say things that we don’t like. We can only live together in that way. And if we are to live together and not die together, we should learn the kind of tolerance which is absolutely vital to the continuation of human life on this planet.”  -- @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro] Not a guru, not a god, just a friendly lill’ line, Just Bertrand, my wise old crush, tapping my mind Says the world is small and the future is near And it only takes two things to save us dear  [Verse 1 (the intellectual thing)] Look at the world with unclouded eyes Not what you wish for, not pretty lies Not what feels good, not what sells or saves Just what is true in the light of the day Let the facts be strange, let them be kind Let them humble your heart and sharpen your mind  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Verse 2 (the moral thing)] This world is crowded and beautifully odd Full of people you’ll never fully applaud Some will annoy you, some will offend But none of us make it alone in the end Love isn’t weak and it isn’t naive It’s the only way any of us get to breathe  [Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Bridge  (true story)] We’re riding one planet through infinite space No spare, no backup, no second place So hold your beliefs with a little bit loose And hold on to each other like it really matters, because, it does  [Final Chorus] Two things, darling, hold them tight Clear in your head, keep love in sight Think like a scientist, act like a true friend Sing like a humanist, make hope matter again  [Outro (when knowsutra slide into growsutra and glowsutra)] If we’re gonna live, we live this way With honest eyes, please don’t look away Cherish the things that sing like a prayer Let’s dare to share just how much we care  🕊️❤️‍🔥

ep_title: A Letter to My Friend (Never Again) EPx44 ☮ GROWsutra World Peace Mantra
description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: This song is a spin off an unreleased song titled “Obscene Profanities”, or maybe “Profane Obscenities”; I still can’t decide, ha. Who knows anyway, and who cares? I only know the insane, toxic spectacle that is the American Administration Ego & Greed Masquerade Gone Bananas makes absolutely no sense; that is the least I can say, I guess. Yet, I can’t help but(t) care, deeply—for the people, and history, truth, justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, you know, logic, progress, and humanity? (God knows) I’m so, so struggling, if only to find the words, the words that match the depth of my dismay, my literal sidération, which TBCH is turning into deeper despair everyday. That much I know I know, I’m afraid. And FWIW, candor is my superpower, and I excel at ruminating, too LOL... Sigh. Ah.   "If We Had But(t) The Truth."  I wrote the song(s) on Easter weekend, after suffering yet again the insanity that is watching (only because he’s overwhelmingly polluting my feeds, no matter how much I don’t want #metoo) FOTUS—aka the only convict rap!st Felon Christian Supremacist Dictator who took the presidential Oath without putting his hand on the Bible—quacking like the shameless, soulless liar he is, acting as pompous as ever, speaking of gratitude and holy afterlife, AS IF!   This EPx5 series could def use some mastering love, but(t) considering the ambient mediocrity, and the fact it’s basically sung with puke in my mouth, I figured, it’s only more authentic this way, ha (I wish I was laughing, I quack you not, butt)…  @bananasutra lyrics:  If we had but the truth,  Not twisted for profit,  If we had but the faith,  Untouched by a wallet,  If we had but the vows,  Still sacred, still solemn,  If we had but the hands,  Unsoiled by gold columns We could maybe still sing,  We could maybe still hope,  We could maybe still breathe,  Through the tightening rope.  If we had but the law,  Not bartered for favors,  If we had but the grace,  Not clutched by defamers,  If we had but the oaths,  Not smirked into silence,  If we had but the cross,  Not wielded with violence We could maybe still stand,  We could maybe still trust,  We could maybe still find  A soul left in the dust.  But instead we have blaspheme,  And a flag wrapped in shame,  And the sacred made market,  And the market made game.  We have pulpits of poison,  We have temples of greed,  We have prayers made of profit,  We have sins without need.  We have kings without conscience,  We have crowns made of lies,  We have scriptures rewritten  By the hungriest eyes.  We have banners of virtue,  Waved by hands that defile,  We have piety pimped out,  To the loudest denial.  If we had but the shame,  If we had but the grief,  If we wept for the ruin,  Not profaned disbelief We might still be obscene,  But we'd know we were wrong.  Instead we call this just another day gone.   Just another day gone...  #deepbreath

description: “Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers—Build your hope on reason’s stairs.”  I love this song very much, and am overdue to share it :) It was inspired by a bold and brilliant essay Bertrand Russell wrote in 1929 (and for fool disclosure, Bertrand is my all-time favorite philosopher, and was also a renowned mathematician; if you're curious, I recommend you check out "The Conquest of Happiness"). His essay aims to answer a question I've asked myself for as long as I can remember, an important one: “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”   His answer? Not really—and certainly not uniquely.... long story short, here's what he concludes: * Compassion doesn’t require dogma. * Progress thrives on questions, not creeds. * Morality rooted in obedience is not morality—it’s fear in disguise.  He believed humanity could find meaning, ethics, and joy through reason, science, and humanism—no gods or thrones required. This song echoes that spirit: a love letter to curiosity, courage, and clarity. A little irreverent, a lot sincere.  --- @bananasutra “Reason Over Reverence” fool lyrics ✨  They built the heavens with fear in the sky, Promised salvation but told us to die. The weight of the world, they placed on their knees, But truth grows in questions, not in decrees.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  They called it wisdom to silence dissent, Made a virtue of guilt and a sin of content. But knowledge is freedom, unchained by creed, No dogma required to learn how to lead.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  No eternal fire, no thrones on high, Just the vast unknown where truths collide. We walk the earth with curious eyes, Finding meaning where wonder lies.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  So let’s build a world where all can explore, Free from the chains of the dogma of yore. For in the search, not the faith, we’ll find, The beauty of life and the power of mind.  ⭐︎⭐︎⭐︎

description: How do you feel about financing neofascism, Murica? Are you feeling dangerously insane yet? I'm asking because, to be completely honest, I dunno what(tf) dissent looks like now—but(t) I'm thinking not paying federal taxes seems like a reasonable, effective way to RESIST authoritarian cruelty, for example. I also desperately wonder why so few are reacting, much less organizing. Why are elected representatives doing what seems to account to basically nothing? Where(tf) are the brave thinkers, the benevolent leaders, the new millennium's progressive Joan of Arc? HOW CAN I HELP?   I dunno, but(t) I dare ask... even with just another BLOWsutra Revolution Ring song of yesterdays and tomorrows gone banana—it’s raw, it’s flawed, bloody dirty goddamn heck, it’s Monday in Murica 🙈🙉🙊🍟   — [Intro] No, it’s not bullshit as usual... The new normal is not neutral. Consent’s just gone, Rights abandoned. Democracy’s dead, Dissent’s gone dread...  [Verse 1 – state surveillance & corporate control] We used to scream into the streets, Now silence starts inside our feeds. They call it bugs… but posts go poof! YouTube’s chat rewrites the truth.  It’s a game of men of shame, History’s a threat to them. Big Tech broke its poker face, Now every scroll’s a hiding place.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: Invisible, internal, thin, A muted thought beneath your skin. It’s algorithms, not a gun, But hun, that’s how new wars are won. This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 2 – systemic institutional sabotage] They gutted justice from its core, Civil servants walked out the door. Philosophy? Deleted. Gone… Because ideas might catch on!  The deans stay quiet, donors cheer. The law’s sold in the name of fear. A government of grift and dare, Where treason hides in legal wear.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: A clause erased, a mail delayed, A syllabus they never made, A lawyer’s oath that’s lost its weight, A student debt that seals a fate… This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 3 – engineered chaos & bots Control] They seed the feeds with farmed out bots, Praise God, and peddle prison plots. The “debates” are traps that loop and stall, Just rage machines to waste us all.  Your logic’s flagged, your truth’s dismissed, While trolls define who can exist. They shoot and fire, then say “calm down”, And blame the victim, as most yawn...  [Bridge – this is not a drill] It’s not a glitch, It’s not a test, It’s policy, A bloody mess!  They want confusion, Promote delusion. They bait with faith, Then fear, then wrath!  Every move is built to break, Not fix, Not free, Not heal, Just take!  [Verse 4 – NO ONE IS SAFE] No trial, no truth, no public proof, No prayer strong enough to soothe. Deport the loud, imprison the poor, Fund new cages, then build some more!  Speak the truth and lose your claim. No jobs, no aids, hopes gone in flame. Their plan is prepped, the script’s in place, And it’s ruthless, death wears no face…  [Final Chorus – the end game, i.e. so what now?] This is what dissent looks like now: A lullaby beneath a drone, A name redacted from a phone, A felon tweeting from hell’s throne.  May we dare scream, cry out loud… This is what dissent looks like now? 🕊️🩸

description: Current mood: revisiting my BLOWsutra "Revolution Ring" songs backlog, to better feel & distill 'em antiantiantifa gems, or something something like huh hope, or something ha... you know? #defy   This JAZZ (side A) + LOFI (side B) release is volume 2 of a 3-songs across 3 sutras EP, asking questions that blow so hard, huh, thank god I can sing—not just rrruminate—'em facts of fasc!sm: 1. KNOWsutra (Naked Truth) - "Shameless", asking aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed, and what are we doing, really? 2. BLOWsutra (Apes Gone Wrong) - "Optics of Cruelty", asking if cruelty is the point, and where the barrel’s aimed tonight? 3. GROWsutra (Dare to Care) - "Universal Currency", asking what's a child worth on the sheet, and how the hell did we get this cold? #truestory 🍌🍔  — Song 1 - KNOWsutra: Shameless  [Verse 1] Didn’t they used to hide the pain? Curtains drawn, lies explained. Now it’s cages on parade, Front row seats and lemonade.  [Verse 2] Spanish moss and razor wire, Swamp gas and a ring of fire. Streaming live from hell’s front porch, Sippin’ pride through plastic straws.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to whisper, now we frame it. History once burned in smoke, Now it’s merch and Facebook jokes. So what are we doing, really? Is this who we are, Or just who we let be?  [Verse 3] Families fenced and tagged by name, Like barcodes marked with blame. You scroll right past the gator’s grin, “Just policy,” with southern spin.  [Bridge] They buried truth, once, deep in code, Now it rides a float down Main Street road.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to hide itnow we claim it. This ain’t justice, it’s a show. Will you clap… or will you go?  [Outro] So tell me plain, if this ain’t war, Why are there camps on freedom’s floor?  — Song 2 - BLOWsutra: Optics of Cruelty  [Verse 1] Do you light the stage with pain? Do you script the bloodstains? Policies dressed up as art, Is that pride… or just a part?  [Verse 2] Is your barrel pointed well? Do you feel divine as people yell? Is your silence sleek and smooth, Like the lies you make look true?  [Chorus] Is it policy… or performance art? Dead kids make a striking chart. You polished boots to match the scene, Who needs gas when you’ve got a screen? Cruelty’s the point, admit it, You choreographed every minute.  [Verse 3] Does the pain make you feel tall? Do you flirt with fascist calls? You don’t stumble… this was built. Goebbels would applaud your guilt.  [Bridge] Zionist or Nazi cap, Doesn’t matter when it’s a trap. Only difference in the fight? Where the barrel’s aimed tonight?  [Chorus] Is it optics, or is it truth? Do you need the proof in youth? Is this theater, is this real, Or just how you love to feel?  [Outro] You don’t lead, you puppeteer. And I see the strings real clear.  — Song 3 - GROWsutra: Universal Currency  [Verse 1] What’s a child worth on the sheet? Not enough to skip elite. Line item, bolded, clean, $109k, no in-between.  [Verse 2] They die in heat, they drown in flood… While suits debate the cost of blood. They say “don’t politicize the pain”, But budgets got a dollar sign for shame.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And decency’s the rate. But y’all keep trading futures For fear, and war, and hate. What do they cost, in flesh and soul? And how the hell did we get this cold?  [Verse 3] A child in Ohio, a girl in the rain, Died while you argued about campaign gain. You priced their breath and called it fair… As if love could balance a billionaire.  [Bridge] Empathy ain’t weak, it’s wealth. It’s everything you kill by stealth.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And we’re bankrupt on the heart. When budgets trump their little lives, We’ve torn the world apart. What are they worth? You tell me straight. Before it’s all too damn late.  [Outro] This ain’t about right or left. It’s about what the soul has left.

tags: Jazz & Blues,gipsy jazz,psychedelic cabaret,acoustic poetry,vocal blues,female tenor,smoky,bluesy,dubby,Indie,authenticity,surreal reality
description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... Blessed be the sound in our bones ✨  EPx16 flow: ❯ Sultry JAZZ (1-2) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (3-5) ❯ Dreamy DUB (6-10) ❯ Indie BURLESQUE (11-14) ❯ Smoky BLUES (15-16)  — @bananasutra “Kiss a Pulse” #songwriter #lyrics  [Verse 1] So many dream of poet’s fame, Celebrate names like some lame game, Wearing words like ego prizes… But joy is awe, not disguises.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Verse 2] To want a name is not enough, To love your life, breathe in the rough. It can’t be faked, to live the beat, Taste the rhythm, embrace the sweet.  [Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue.  [Bridge] Why claim titles, rather than dance? Seek magic truths, imagine chance… Each breath’s a rhyme, each stumble, art, Nurture ‘em sparkles in your heart.  [Outro] Be the poem, feel its grace, Explore shadows, shine in space, Forget titles, laughing at thrones… Blessed be the song in our bones.  — Still reading? Yay. You may also like the sister song I released as a single about a year ago: "She Wears the Words  • JAZZsutra Mighty Poetry Minute" ❤️‍🔥

track title: [06] Sing Your Own Gospel • GROWsutra (God, Etc.) Gipsy Bass JAZZ
ep_title: Sing Your Own Gospel • Vol. 2 EPx7 • GROWsutra (God · Etc) Revolutionary Gipsy JAZZ
description: “Sing Your Own Gospel”, GROWsutra (God, Etc.) is a sister song of “Make your Own Bible”, and what my bananasutra project really is all about—inspired by a fine American thinker, sir Ralph Waldo Emerson, who wisely advised: “Make your Own Bible. Select and collect all the words and sentences that in all your readings have been to you like the blast of a trumpet.” 🎺⛓️‍💥  I mean… your call, of course! But(t) if you’re curious, Rousseau and Russel are great preachers daddies in a world gone bananas, etc... #nowyouknow  •  •  •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Verse 1] I searched for God in ‘em Holy Books, But all I found was some preachers hooks. So I built a church in my own mind, With no pews, no pride, kind words that rhyme.  [Chorus] Sing your Gospel, like it’s a magic wand, A blast of truth, feel it, it’s grand! In the Bible of Us, we’re all just human, Dancing alone, lost in wonderland.  [Verse 2] I read Rousseau and Russel with a glass of red, Jean Paul Sartre and Camus in my bed. Why obey rules from the days of old? I’ll craft my truth in stories bold.  [Chorus] Sing your own Gospel, write your own song, Find where you’re right, admit when you’re wrong. In the Bible of truth, there’s more than one tune, Wink at the stars, and laugh with the moon.  [Bridge] Life’s a cabaret, a silly little dance, Between fate and free will, a game of chance. No need for a savior, damn holy decree, Just the jazz in our soul, setting us free.  [Chorus] Sing your own Gospel, dance with your doubts, Whisper your secrets, and scream them out loud. In the Bible of trust, let’s find our own truths, Lost in the rhythm, defying our youth.  [Outro] Yeah let’s write our scriptures, line by line, Oh that book of life, it’s goddamn divine. No priest, no prophet, just the truths we dare speak, In this holy cabaret, we don’t fear the meek. •  •  •

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: "It's an Ethical Paradox, an Oxymoron Maze" Vol. 2 EPx15 is a gipsy jazz edit of a dense KNOWsutra (Bertrand Knows) song that still needs some distilling, and so here it flows, from Burlesque Jazzzzzzzzz (1-10) to Gipsy LoFi (11-14) to Indie DUB (15)...  Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals" essay, where he asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?"   In this controversial essay, he made the fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh? Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah! In fact, Bertrand concluded the following: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (!) (Marriage and Morals)  And if you're doubting the veracity and value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions and observations, here's a fun fact for ya: marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world, until the mid-90s?! (GASP)  • • •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Verse 1] Step right up to the paradox parade, Where the morals they sell come double-edged blade. They wag their fingers, legislate laws, Then break ’em in private to polite applause.  It’s a sugar-spun circus, bananas on stage, Where yes means no and restraint’s just a phrase. Marriage or market, they blur the scene, Stamp it “righteous”, don’t ask what it means.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Verse 2] In the chapel it’s sacred, divinely endowed, In the alley it’s vulgar, condemned out loud. One buys a mattress, one buys a ring, Different costumes, same bargaining.  They preach purity, polish the lie, While need’s the product they monetize. Suit and tie or a scarlet brand, Same old hustle… supply, demand.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Bridge] Here’s a riddle, let logic stew: Who makes the crime, then blames it on you? They build the cage, lock the lid, Then curse the creature they forbid.  [Verse 3] Russell saw it, cut clean through the fog, Truth gets strangled by moral smog. Love’s not a contract, priced or policed, It’s a living thing begging for release.  Burn the scripts that barter the heart, Let freedom finish what law couldn’t start. No paradox, no moral sleight, Just justice breathing in open light.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Outro] Fold up the map, walk out the maze, No room for riddles in love’s next phase. The ethical circus packs up its tent, Let truth be simple, that’s how it’s meant. • • •

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise. They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there.  [Verse 2 — The Great Goons] A buffoon tweets from a gilded throne, While loyal goons praise what ain’t shown, They bow and swear, “Oh, it’s divine!” Then clap along in crooked time.  Echoes ring through hollow halls, Truth gets lost beneath applause, Every doubt gets dipped in gold, Every lie gone wild and old.  [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking.  Oh let us laugh and let it ring, At paper crowns and cha-ching, The grandest show of empty things, All hail the king of nothing.  [Verse 3 — Hello Charlie Chaplin] ’Til one small voice broke through the swing, Soft and kind like Chaplin would sing, “This dicktator is a cheat,” And tender hearts skipped a beat.  A whisper cut through all the noise, Simple truth with humble poise, And for a breath the spell grew thin, Like light was finally let in.  [Bridge — Say no to Complicity] What a vast hallucination, Built on fear and fabrication, Pure race, pure flag, pure vanity, A costume stitched in complicity. [Chorus — Blessed Be Fools] Oh let us laugh at what we see, The Great Naked King in pageantry, Wearing nothing but bling-bling, Oh, if only I was joking. description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

In this controversial essay, he made the fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh? Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah! In fact, Bertrand concluded the following: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (!) (Marriage and Morals)  And if you're doubting the veracity and value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions and observations, here's a fun fact for ya: marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world, until the mid-90s?! (GASP)  • • •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Verse 1] Step right up to the paradox parade, Where the morals they sell come double-edged blade. They wag their fingers, legislate laws, Then break ’em in private to polite applause.  It’s a sugar-spun circus, bananas on stage, Where yes means no and restraint’s just a phrase. Marriage or market, they blur the scene, Stamp it “righteous”, don’t ask what it means.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Verse 2] In the chapel it’s sacred, divinely endowed, In the alley it’s vulgar, condemned out loud. One buys a mattress, one buys a ring, Different costumes, same bargaining.  They preach purity, polish the lie, While need’s the product they monetize. Suit and tie or a scarlet brand, Same old hustle… supply, demand.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Bridge] Here’s a riddle, let logic stew: Who makes the crime, then blames it on you? They build the cage, lock the lid, Then curse the creature they forbid.  [Verse 3] Russell saw it, cut clean through the fog, Truth gets strangled by moral smog. Love’s not a contract, priced or policed, It’s a living thing begging for release.  Burn the scripts that barter the heart, Let freedom finish what law couldn’t start. No paradox, no moral sleight, Just justice breathing in open light.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Outro] Fold up the map, walk out the maze, No room for riddles in love’s next phase. The ethical circus packs up its tent, Let truth be simple, that’s how it’s meant. • • •

ep_title: A Letter to My Friend (Never Again) EPx44 ☮ GROWsutra World Peace Mantra
description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

ep_title: A Letter to My Friend (Never Again) EPx44 ☮ GROWsutra World Peace Mantra
description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: Cassandra’s Lullaby is an EPx11 that blends Jewish jazz, gypsy dub, and trip-hop into a sparse, analog landscape of truths denied and raw emotions... It’s a haunting, mythical torch song for the age of forgetting, a poetic letter to a friend, and a warning to the world. I’ll pray that grace breaks through your slumber, And helps the world unclose its eyes.  May your heart unclose with grace… And prove you’re more than a fart’s face.

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: “Question the Nation” is inspired by beat poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti’s “Pity the Nation” poem (after Khalil Gibran), filtered through my candid, thoughtful skepticism, and fiery, psychedelic truth-seeking lens—i.e. the bananasutra philosophy of what designing a meaningful & honest life in a sustainable & happy world is all about. I don’t claim to have answers, but I refuse to silence fair questions that matter; and, I sincerely care to invite you to pay attention, too!   — @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] Question the nation… Hallucinate salvation… Where truth took a vacation… Bananasutra vibration…  [Verse 1] Who sold your soul at the discount mall? Who scrolls your dreams through the data sprawl? Who doctored your doubt with dopamine drip? Who coded your faith with a censorship script?  Who profits from panic, post after post? Who sells your fear for the likes they host? Who filters your pain till it looks aesthetic? Who turns your silence into something prophetic?  [Chorus] Question the nation, hear the narration, Dystopian salvation, mad fornication. Bananasutra, peel seducer, Fruit opener, pulse creator.  [Verse 2] Who digs ’em dicks of breaking bad news? Who hid the despair in patriotic hues? Who cheered the bully, called it divine? Who whispered “freedom” while drawing the line?  Who buried the poets in bureaucrat dust? Who trademarked love and privatized trust? Who voted progress, forgot the soul? Who took the toll just to play a role?  [Chorus] Question the nation, denounce corruption, Peace detonation, fair migration. Bananasutra, mantra mover, Dubbed-up Buddha, groove improver.  [Bridge] Who sleeps sound when the sirens cry? description: This is a French (my mother tongue) EPx17 song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”…   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting and relevant psychological insights:   “One of the saddest lessons of history is this:  If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

[Chorus] Who writes the rain, or signs the sky? Who dreams needing a reason why? Blush deep, kiss a pulse, hum a song, Feel the flavors roll off your tongue. description: “Rage bait” was named the 2025 Word of the Year by the Oxford dictionary, and frankly, it’s no surprise. We are witnessing a grotesque circus of injustice—a global crisis that leaves many of us feeling powerless against the cold, cruel gears of the so-called new world order. And I, for one, often find myself holding my breath, standing at the edge of an increasingly scary, angry, insane lose-lose reality…  I wrote “One Percent Rising” almost a year ago, as a sort of torch song for the Curious, the Honest, and the Unseen. Inspired by a deep-dive personality test that placed me in "the top 1% of Curiosity", this song is a reminder of how rare and vital Universalism, Humility, and Authenticity have become; how much they matter, in a world that feels like a deadly toxic "hog-feed" of manufactured noise, led by "suits and ties" high on ego, fear, and conformity. It’s meant to be like a spark in the fog, for me, and for you, and everyone, equally… if you dare to care ;) Think of it as a lill’ pep talk, a friendly 'n fresh breath of hope, to feed sensitive and sensible souls—a prayer of sorts, for Creative (r)Evolution.   With this song, I want to encourage prioritizing curiosity over competition, and sincerity over status, to help us feel like we can rise above this fasc!st tsunami... while others brainlessly and heartlessly admire and rewards nefarious ”Power Hoarders", like a herd of ignorant "Conformity Bros”, aka sheeples... Because, in an era gone fool on backward bananas—where global fascist trends and dehumanizing antics posture as “smart”, glorifying deceit in the name of greed—what we need, to solve dire problems, to survive, essentially, is a hell of a lot of imagination, rooted in altruism. I believe that with all my KNOWing and BLOWing guts! description: Just another WTF song, I reckon 🍌 EPx10 flows Accordion 🪗 ❯ Cello Bass Guitar 🎻 ❯ Piano 🎹  Please pardon my French, and enjoy the absurd waltz circus des secrets de polichinelles--it's like a gipsy burlesque chanson show, a story about  dystopian abuse (of all kinds) is increasingly being normalized, here and there and again, as we (the people, women in particular) are being dehumanized... yet (the worst part) people be like shhh 🤫  🎪  🎪  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro]  Chut...  Fais comme si t’savais pas,  Fais comme si t’voyais pas,  Le roi est nu, mais quelle classe, n’est-ce pas ?  [Couplet 1]  Sous la dentelle des fashos,  On cache les corps, on cache les mots,  On peint la guerre couleur d’amour,  Et les bourreaux jouent les troubadours.  La foi prêche la décence,  Les fous vendent la délivrance,  Et les rois font la révérence  À leurs propres violences.  [Refrain]  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Le monde tourne à la ficelle.  On bénit l’ordre, on brûle l’ciel,  Au nom du bien, des seins, oh hell…  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Tout l’monde ment, tout l’monde est belle.  On rit, on pleure, on s’fait la belle,  Sous la loi des criminels.  [Couplet 2]  On dit “paix” pour vendre des bombes,  On dit “mère” pour taire les tombes,  On dit “libre” pour mieux soumettre,  Et “Dieu” pour justifier le maître.  Les hommes de loi, les femmes de honte,  Les vieilles idoles qu’on remonte,  Les dieux, les lois, les vieilles montres,  Tous décalés d’un monde qui s’démonte.   [Refrain]  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Le monde tourne à la ficelle.  On bénit l’ordre, on brûle l’ciel,  Au nom du bien, des seins, oh hell…  C’est un secret de Polichinelle…  On s’embrasse, on fait la belle,  Comme des culs qui se querellent,  Danse ma sœur, pense infidèle.  [Pont]  Fais-moi croire encore un peu,  Que le silence est vertueux,  Que l’obéissance est glorieuse,  Et que la foi n’est pas dangereuse…  Mais chut... le cirque recommence,  Marionnettes en transe,  Et sous la piste, les consciences  Qui s’embrasent en connivence. C’est un secret de Polichinelle…  Sous la jupe du mensonge universel,  J’cache ma rage et mon appel,  Pour un monde moins artificiel.  [Outro]  Chut...  Tout le monde sait, Mais personne ne dit rien.  C’est bien plus commode… Et puis, plus inhumain...  🃏🍌

description: Ce qui est marrant c'est que salaud au féminin, en français, c'est pas salaude! Ha, #justsayin Chanson inspirée par un vrai livre recent intitulé "Le Temp Des Salauds" 🍟🤓🤌  @bananasutra lyrics (variantions):  [Intro] Bienvenue, mesdames et messieurs,  Au grand bal des vertus douteuses.  Ici, les salauds dansent heureux,  Les cœurs vendus, les mains soyeuses.  Leur morale est bien repassée,  Mais toujours un peu tachée.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds, Des faux héros, des pantins d’ego,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  C’est le temps des salauds, oh-oh,  Des beaux parleurs, des faux normaux,  Qui rient très haut… pour mentir plus beau.  [Couplet 1 – Le délire raisonnable] Le nouveau réalisme, c’est l’art des salauds,  Un délirium sobre, cynisme en costard chaud.  Ils vendent la peur sous cellophane,  Et t’appellent “extrême” si tu dis “humain”.  Ils posent des questions de sages,  Mais répondent comme des mirages sauvages.  Ils jouent à la raison...  mais raisonnent faux,  C’est la saison, la moisson des salauds.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des cerveaux trop clos,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  [Couplet 2 – Les alliances du vide] Trois types de salauds, faut l’dire clair:  Les politiques, les patrons, les faiseurs d’prières.  Ceux qui savent mais trahissent,  Eux les lâches, qui profitent.  Le p’tit Jupiter, Machiavel au moral,  Fait valser les foules dans son bal libéral.  Il pactise, il nuance, tord le vrai,  Pour qu’le faux paraisse sensé.  [Pont] Forts avec les faibles, faibles avec les forts,  Ils vendent la paix pendant qu’ils signent la mort.  “Bon courage”, qu’ils disent, le sourire faux,  Mais c’est un orage… on danse, salauds?  [Couplet 3 – Les fous et les faux] Les fous aboient, les salauds cadrent,  Et les cons signent tous les contrats.  Les uns hurlent, les autres calculent,  Et les lucides… se taisent, s’annulent.  Les idoles changent, les valeurs se vendent,  La foule like, la vérité s’attend.  Les héros sont devenus salauds,  Nous, figurants d’un online show.  [Refrain – Final] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des gros egos,  Qui valsent au rythme des fiascos,  Au bal, au bal des salauds! (oh-oh)  Au bal… des salauds.  [Outro] J’en ai aimé, des salauds, c’est vrai,  Leurs mots brillants, leurs airs parfaits.  Mais minuit sonne, le bal s’oublie,  Ces salauds-là ne dansent plus… avec ma vie.

description: This is a French (my mother tongue) EPx17 song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”…   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting and relevant psychological insights:   “One of the saddest lessons of history is this:  If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

[Pont] Forts avec les faibles, faibles avec les forts,  Ils vendent la paix pendant qu’ils signent la mort.  “Bon courage”, qu’ils disent, le sourire faux,  Mais c’est un orage… on danse, salauds? description: When brutal force is normalized, we the people are dehumanized. Please don't let 'em power hungry cowards stampede our peace with greedy double-standards and manipulative lies, because peace is everything... and being honest, vulnerable, and fair is being brave.   Ça je le sais, dans mon coeur. Et le rêve qui m'anime, il est fait de paix et d'amour sans peur.  Artistic expression is my Force Douce. And it ain’t a skill, or an asset, it’s a gift, to you and me!  Making music ain’t about ego, nor fame, or #godforbid money, #corporatebranding or #copyrights it ain’t even really about hard work, nor what buttons one pushes, or what strings one plucks—it is about intentional exploration, about pulling the invisible yet super awesome magic strings only brave pure loving #souls dare to share, as we leap forward, trusting we’re all here to learn aka evolve, grateful we’re all born equal, as divinely mighty as fragile, i.e. #human 💌  ✪ ✪ ✪  “La Force Douce” @bananasutra #lyrics en Français:   [Couplet 1] Il faut être bien malheureux  pour semer la douleur sans raison, pour étouffer la lumière d’un cœur  par simple trahison.  Mais moi j’ai vu que la paix,  c’est pas la fuite ni la peur, c’est un feu tranquille,  un courage qui guérit nos rancœurs.  [Pré-refrain] Ils disent que la bonté c’est faible,  moi je dis c’est divin, regarde les rivières:  elles creusent la pierre,  sans jamais lever la main.  [Refrain] Bananasutra  chante la force douce, celle qui choisit d’aimer  quand tout s’écroule autour.  Bananasutra,  les âmes justes avancent nues, intègres, vulnérables,  mais debout jusqu’au bout.  [Couplet 2] Il faut être bien audacieux  pour parler vrai sans armure, montrer ses cicatrices  comme des fleurs sous la blessure.  Justice, ce n’est pas la vengeance,  c’est l’équilibre des vents, où chacun gagne en donnant,  où l’humain devient vivant.  [Pont] Quand le monde crie “gagne seul”,  je réponds “gagnons ensemble”, le futur n’est pas une guerre,  c’est un chant qu’on assemble.  L’amour n’est pas dangereux,  c’est la seule loi qui sauve, et la tendresse,  c’est l’arme des braves.  [Refrain] Bananasutra, dans le feu des jours, tu gardes la foi, tu redonnes l’amour. Bananasutra, même au bord du monde, ta paix rayonne, et jamais ne succombe.  [Outro] Il faut être bien pernicieux  pour punir sans comprendre, mais il faut être divinement fou  pour continuer d’aimer tendre.  —  "The Gentle Force” lyrics in English (unedited AI translation, for the curious :)  [Verse 1] You have to be very unhappy To sow pain for no reason, To stifle the light of a heart By simple betrayal.  But I saw that peace, It's not flight or fear, It's a quiet fire, A courage that heals our grudges.  [Pre-crorus] They say that goodness is weak, I say it's divine, Look at the rivers: They dig the stone, Without ever raising your hand.  [Chorus] Bananasutra Sings the gentle force, The one who chooses to love When everything collapses around.  Bananasutra, The righteous souls advance naked, Honest, vulnerable, But standing until the end.  [Verse 2] You have to be very bold To speak the truth without armor, Show your scars Like flowers under the wound.  Justice is not revenge, It's the balance of the winds, Where everyone wins by giving, Where the human becomes alive.  [Bridge] When the world shouts "win alone", I answer "we win together", The future is not a war, It's a song that we put together.  Love is not dangerous, It's the only law that saves, And tenderness, It's the weapon of the brave.  [Chorus] Bananasutra, in the fire of days, You keep the faith, you give back the love. Bananasutra, even at the edge of the world, Your peace radiates, and never succumbs.  [Outro] You have to be very pernicious To punish without understanding, But you have to be divinely crazy To continue to love tender.

description: “Synthema Sutra” is a nerdy banana philosophy explainer song, with no hooky hook, no catchy catch, no morale of the story even... It just asks what if Sutras were ancient Greek Synthemas, and strolls through each Sutra, one by one (KNOW, BLOW, SHOW, GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW). One song, seven guiding principles, and a bunch of gods who totally would have benefited from #musictherapy :) Enjoy the melodic wander. Or don’t. Whatever works for ya. The gods won’t agree about it anyway, haha #truestory  EPx8 flows Indie (1), LoFi (2-3), Dub (4), Burlesque (5-7), and psychedelic Indie Punk Rock (8).  And if you're a Greek mythology nerd, or just curious about the ancient wisdom of musical storytelling gone bananas, or both, here's the split 🍌🏛️ 1. KNOWsutra : Prometheus ➵ Gave fire (knowledge) to humans; punished for empowering truth. A true win-win rebel. 2. BLOWsutra : Hydra + Medusa ➵ Hydra: corrupt systems that grow stronger when attacked wrong. Medusa: demonized femininity + misunderstood power. 3. SHOWsutra : Dionysus ➵ God of ecstatic joy, chaos, music, and theatre. Shows the sacred side of silliness and subversion. 4. FLOWsutra : Hermes ➵ Trickster god of transitions, language, and messages. A master of in-betweenness. 5. GROWsutra : Persephone ➵ Her cycle (abduction and return) teaches growth through descent and rebirth. Feminine resilience myth. 6. GLOWsutra : Apollo + Hestia ➵ Apollo = light, art, and healing. Hestia = the hearth, peace, inner warmth. 7. BOWsutra : Orpheus ➵ Music so beautiful it moved the gods. Journeyed to the underworld for love—faith, failure, and awe.  ♆♆♆ @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1 – KNOW : Prometheus] Every truth you KNOW   Flickers soft and low   Like a stolen flame   From a god of shame   He gave us fire, paid the toll   To free the know from control    [Verse 2 – BLOW / Hydra + Medusa] Every cruel BLOW   Feeds the beast below   Cut one head, three rise   In the name of lies   And still we cage her rage and grace   To fear what dares to blow this place    [Verse 3 – SHOW : Dionysus ] Every mask you SHOW   Hides the pain you stow   But the sacred jest   Is a truth confessed   He laughs through wounds the wise won’t see   To show what dares to set us free    [Verse 4 – GROW : Persephone] Every time you GROW   You descend below   Like the seeds she sows   Where the silence knows   That roots need dark to rise again   And grow through loss, not just through gain    [Verse 5 – FLOW : Hermes ] Every word you FLOW   Is a place you go   Past the borderlines   Of the gods' designs   Hermes walks where logic ends   To let new meanings flow through bends    [Verse 6 – GLOW : Apollo + Hestia ] Every time you GLOW   Through the ache and slow   You become the spark   In the temple dark   He sings the wounds she warms to heal   They glow in silence, soft and real    [Verse 7 – BOW : Orpheus ] Every time you BOW   To the here and now   Like Orpheus did   For the love he hid   You trust the gods to give it back   But some truths die when we bow to lack    [Outro] Synthema… Sutra…   We know… we blow…   We show… we grow…   We flow… we glow…   And sometimes… we bow…    ♆♆♆

Vivir sin pruebas, sin ego, sin balanza   Construir puentes sobre grietas falsas   Y ver magia en cada paso de esperanza    Lo sabes cuando la ves, cuando fluye   Esa voz poética, cruda, que influye   Canta sentido, conexión y asombro   Y a veces hasta hace vibrar el corazón hondo    (Creo) Porque capta texturas humanas profundas   Pinta belleza en diferencias fecundas   Más allá de cañones y culturas   No es disfraz, es verdad sin censura    Es lenguaje humilde hecho de lo diario   Que demuestra ser sagrado y necesario   Llena el vacío de una voz que abraza   Como que amar es dios, y cantar no se rechaza    (Creo) Por eso la poesía es necesidad   Un medio, un lenguaje para esta nueva edad   Un camino al alma, la dignidad   Un canto de vida, belleza y verdad
